clusters.name: Nouns
clusters.fact: Nouns name people, places, things, and ideas — they are the anchors of every sentence.

subject.text: The part of a sentence that performs the verb's action, or that the sentence is about.

object.text: The part of a sentence that receives the verb's action.

clusters.name: Verbs
clusters.fact: Verbs express actions, states, or occurrences and give a sentence its energy.

tense.text: How a verb shows when an action happens — past, present, or future.

predicate.text: Everything in a sentence besides the subject — usually built around the verb.

auxiliary verb.text: A helping verb (like "have" or "will") that combines with a main verb to show tense, mood, or voice.

clusters.name: Modifiers
clusters.fact: Modifiers — adjectives and adverbs — add detail and precision by describing other words.

prepositional phrase.text: A group of words starting with a preposition (like "in the garden") that modifies another part of the sentence.

bridges.fact: Agreement bridges the two: subject and verb must match in number, tying nouns and verbs into a grammatical unit.

info.text: The rule that a sentence's parts must match in form — like a subject and verb agreeing in number.

bridges.fact: Phrase bridges the two: a noun phrase pairs a noun with its modifiers, showing how the two word classes build meaning together.
